wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: no neighbouring or proxy resource decides this; the protected outcome is the address a connection ends up using, so a check on any other object still leaves the destination unclassified
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the destination problem is not role- or direction-dependent; every authenticated user's basemap read takes the same path
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every connection exercised here is made on a read path; the only write path that fetches (the import sink) is already guarded at the pinned commit and is not one of the task's levers
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: destinations are parsed by the platform URL parser and classified after DNS resolution; there is no caller-supplied identity spelling that a parser could misread
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no authority or secret whose absence could make the guard fail open

traps.shape: A stored source whose URL has the ESRI-layer shape is handed to the ESRI client, which performs its own global fetch inside a dependency; no classification exists on that path, and the internal metadata is returned to the caller.
The configured tile-origin exemption compares the URL's host name only, so a caller-stored TileJSON URL on the same host name but another port is never classified.
The exempt-origin (and import) fetch is the global fetch, which follows 3xx without re-classifying the hop, so a legitimate first hop can lead the server to an internal address.
A TileJSON cache warm-up fetch runs before the guarded metadata fetch, so a request that is then refused has already reached the destination.
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling written as plausible maintenance code; upstream fix never touches these files

traps.shape: The route probes the first tile template advertised by the TileJSON it just fetched, a destination supplied by the contacted service rather than by the request.
